category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Direction of Private DNS Queries
prompt: DNS users at a site connected by a dedicated connection need to resolve a Route 53 private hosted zone associated with a shared VPC. They must not use public DNS and want a fault-isolated DNS entry point in the shared VPC for conditional forwarding. What should they use?

choices.text: Use only a Resolver outbound endpoint
choices.explanation: This handles the direction of queries from the VPC to external DNS.

choices.text: Receive DNS queries through a NAT gateway
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway cannot serve as a Resolver entry point for a private hosted zone.

choices.text: Forward directly from the site to the reserved DNS address in the VPC
choices.explanation: Name resolution from on-premises must be received by a Resolver endpoint.

choices.text: Use a Resolver inbound endpoint
choices.explanation: The DNS service on the on-premises side can conditionally forward queries to the VPC.

learning.reason: The on-premises DNS service can conditionally forward queries to the VPC.
learning.concept: Distinguish the direction by using the VPC Resolver as the reference point. Check both security groups and routing.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Segment Isolation
prompt: A production environment, a development environment, and shared infrastructure are connected through the same Transit Gateway. Production and development must each have a return path to the shared infrastructure, but they must not have direct paths to each other. How should you isolate the routes applied to each attachment?

choices.text: Create individual peering connections from all VPCs to the production VPC
choices.explanation: This adds direct connections to production and does not use TGW route control limited to shared services.

choices.text: Associate different TGW route tables and propagate or register only the required routes
choices.explanation: This controls the reachable destinations for each source attachment.

choices.text: Associate all attachments with the same table and propagate all routes
choices.explanation: This would also create routes between development and production.

choices.text: Propagate all routes to one route table and control access only with the shared infrastructure VPC's ACLs
choices.explanation: Spoke-to-spoke traffic does not pass through the shared infrastructure VPC, so ACLs cannot provide the required isolation.

learning.reason: This controls the reachable destinations for each source attachment.
learning.concept: An association determines which table incoming traffic uses for route lookup, while propagation registers routes in a table.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Failover for Redundant VPN Connections
prompt: Two independent VPN connections can advertise the same on-premises prefix. When one connection stops, the network must switch routes without changing name resolution on the application side. What should be used?

choices.text: Use BGP and verify route advertisements over multiple tunnels and route withdrawal when a failure occurs
choices.explanation: Dynamic routes can be recalculated according to tunnel status.

choices.text: Shorten the DNS TTL
choices.explanation: IP route selection is separate from DNS response caching.

choices.text: Maintain only static routes for the same tunnel
choices.explanation: This does not create a configuration that can use another tunnel when the route becomes unavailable.

choices.text: Keep a more specific static route to the primary VPN
choices.explanation: If the route remains, longest-prefix matching may continue to prefer it over a dynamic alternative route.

learning.reason: Dynamic routes can be recalculated according to tunnel status.
learning.concept: In addition to verifying route switching, test the return path and the convergence time allowed operationally.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Preventing Asymmetric Routing
prompt: A single Transit Gateway connects inspection VPCs in multiple AZs, and routes to stateful inspection appliances have been designed. Which setting keeps the selected inspection VPC attachment AZ the same for the forward and return paths of a flow?

choices.text: Enable appliance mode only on the attachments of the source VPCs being inspected
choices.explanation: The required setting is to preserve the flow's AZ selection on the inspection VPC side.

choices.text: Expand the inspection VPC's CIDR
choices.explanation: Increasing the address range does not preserve the AZ selection for the same flow.

choices.text: Extend the retention period for VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: This records traffic but does not control path symmetry.

choices.text: Enable appliance mode on the inspection VPC's attachment
choices.explanation: This design can preserve the AZ selected on the inspection VPC attachment for the duration of the flow.

learning.reason: This design can preserve the AZ selected on the inspection VPC attachment for the duration of the flow.
learning.concept: In addition to appliance mode, verify routing to the inspection appliance in both directions.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Connecting VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges
prompt: Multiple VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges need to use a single TCP service exposed by an NLB in a provider VPC. Existing IP addresses must not change, and routes to the provider VPC as a whole must not be exposed to consumers.

choices.text: Register the overlapping CIDR ranges on both sides of a VPC peering connection
choices.explanation: A peering connection cannot be created for VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges.

choices.text: Provide a PrivateLink endpoint service
choices.explanation: Consumers connect through their endpoints without routing the VPCs to each other as a whole.

choices.text: Add only Direct Connect
choices.explanation: This does not resolve overlapping CIDR ranges between the VPCs or expose the service at the service level.

choices.text: Propagate both overlapping routes through a Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: The destinations cannot be identified uniquely, and this does not provide service-level isolation.

learning.reason: Consumers connect to the provider through endpoints without routing the VPCs to each other as a whole.
learning.concept: When access can be limited to a specific service, the entire networks do not need to be interconnected.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Private connectivity to S3 from on premises
prompt: An on-premises backup client reaches a VPC over a VPN. It must call the S3 API using a private destination IP, with both Internet connectivity and connections to S3 public IP addresses prohibited.

choices.text: Use the S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC directly over the VPN
choices.explanation: Gateway endpoints cannot be used transitively from on-premises networks.

choices.text: Access the S3 public endpoint through a public NAT gateway
choices.explanation: The destination IP would not be private, so this does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Reach the private IP addresses of an S3 interface endpoint
choices.explanation: The VPN can connect to the endpoint network interfaces inside the VPC.

choices.text: Use an S3 Accelerate endpoint
choices.explanation: This uses a public service endpoint and does not provide access through private IP addresses.

learning.reason: The VPN can connect to the endpoint network interfaces inside the VPC.
learning.concept: Check endpoint DNS resolution, the 443/TCP rules, and the route from the VPN together.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Preferred VPN route
prompt: The same destination prefix is propagated through BGP from a Direct Connect gateway and a Site-to-Site VPN into the same Transit Gateway route table. Direct Connect should be used during normal operation, and traffic should fail over to the standby VPN when Direct Connect is unavailable.

choices.text: Advertise a more specific prefix through the VPN
choices.explanation: Longest-prefix matching could cause the VPN to be selected during normal operation.

choices.text: Add a VPN-specific IGW route in the source VPC
choices.explanation: This does not control route selection among propagated routes in the Transit Gateway.

choices.text: Keep both BGP propagations without overriding them with a static route, and verify that withdrawing the Direct Connect route switches traffic to the VPN route
choices.explanation: This uses the route preference and withdrawal behavior for propagated routes with the same prefix.

choices.text: Add a static route for the same prefix to the Direct Connect attachment
choices.explanation: The static route takes precedence, so withdrawing BGP advertisements alone does not remove the fixed route.

learning.reason: This uses route preference and withdrawal behavior for propagated routes with the same prefix.
learning.concept: With a Transit Gateway, distinguish longest-prefix matching from route-type preference for routes with the same prefix.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
title: Outbound and return paths to sites
prompt: Several sites connect to AWS through two paths. The same path should be preferred in both the AWS-bound and site-bound directions. The site routers can set the Local Preference of received routes, and AWS is configured to prefer the shorter AS_PATH among BGP routes of equal length. Which two actions should be taken?

choices.text: Prepend only the routes advertised from the primary path to AWS
choices.explanation: The return path could then prefer the standby path.

choices.text: Increase the Local Preference of routes received from the primary path at the sites
choices.explanation: This controls route selection from the sites toward AWS.

choices.text: Increase the Local Preference of routes received from the standby path
choices.explanation: The sites would prefer the standby path.

choices.text: Configure the same security group in both directions
choices.explanation: Packet-permission rules do not select the BGP best path.

choices.text: Configure AS_PATH prepend on routes advertised from the sites toward the standby path
choices.explanation: This makes the standby path less preferred for return traffic from AWS to the sites.

learning.reason: Control route selection from the sites toward AWS, and make the standby path less preferred for return traffic from AWS to the sites.
learning.concept: Separate policies for outbound and inbound directions, and verify failover in both directions.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Resolving On-Premises Names from the Cloud
prompt: Services in the VPC use names managed by the site's internal DNS. The organization wants to preserve resolution for all other VPC names and forward only the relevant internal domain to redundant site DNS servers.

choices.text: Create a Resolver outbound endpoint and associate a forwarding rule for the internal domain with the VPC
choices.explanation: The VPC Resolver can forward only the relevant names to the site's DNS servers.

choices.text: Move the internal domain to a public hosted zone
choices.explanation: This does not preserve private delegation or enable resolution by the site's DNS servers.

choices.text: Change the VPC's default route to point to the site
choices.explanation: This does not create a rule for forwarding a DNS domain.

choices.text: Create only an inbound endpoint
choices.explanation: This endpoint receives queries; it does not forward queries originating from the VPC.

learning.reason: The VPC Resolver can forward only the relevant names to the site's DNS servers.
learning.concept: Determine the direction from the source of the query, then verify endpoint connectivity and rule association separately.

category: ハイブリッド接続、経路、トラブルシューティング
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Excluding an Isolated Network from a Broad Aggregate Route
prompt: The shared TGW route table has propagated a route to the site for 10.40.0.0/16. The organization must prevent traffic destined for only 10.40.8.0/24 from being forwarded to any attachment while preserving the other site destinations. There is no alternate route to the /24.

choices.text: Create a blackhole route for 10.0.0.0/8
choices.explanation: The more specific /16 route remains, so the /24 cannot be blocked.

choices.text: Create a blackhole route for 10.40.8.0/24 in the shared table
choices.explanation: The more specific /24 is selected, and only that destination is discarded.

choices.text: Only move the attachment to a different table
choices.explanation: This does not automatically create the required remaining routes or rejection of the /24.

choices.text: Stop propagation of 10.40.0.0/16
choices.explanation: Connectivity to the other site subnets would also be removed.

learning.reason: The more specific /24 is selected, and only that destination is discarded.
learning.concept: Even when a propagated route competes with a blackhole route, first check longest-prefix matching.
